name: Yarlam Resort
summary: Lachung's most upscale hotel, on the hillside above the village with 27 rooms and 3 suites, a spa, gym and a guests-only restaurant. It is the one genuinely premium base for Yumthang and a favourite for honeymooners and older travellers who want warmth and quiet.
body: Yarlam stands on a slope above Lachung, looking down over the town and across the valley, with fir and rhododendron forest around it. Guidebooks and travel writers have long described it as the most luxurious place to stay in Lachung. It has 27 rooms and 3 suites in a single large building, a spa, a gym, a games room and a restaurant, the Guras, for resident guests, serving North Indian, Chinese and continental food.

For North Sikkim, where most rooms are simple, the difference is warmth, space and service after a long, cold day. That matters most to couples on a honeymoon, older travellers and families who want one comfortable night before or after the dawn run to Yumthang. Like every hotel in the valley, it depends on the road being open, and it was affected by the closures of 2023–2025. Check current status before you travel.
why: The most comfortable rooms in Lachung, with valley views
Spa and in-house restaurant after the long drive
Quiet hillside location away from the highway
watch_out: It sits above the main village, so you depend on the hotel or your driver for transport, and rates are several times those of family hotels nearby.

faqs.q: Is Yarlam Resort the best hotel in Lachung
faqs.a: It is widely described as the most luxurious in Lachung, with 27 rooms, 3 suites, a spa and a guests-only restaurant. Whether it is best for you depends on budget: family hotels cost a fraction of the price for a single night. For honeymoons and older travellers, the extra comfort is worth it.

faqs.q: How much does Yarlam Resort cost
faqs.a: Expect roughly ₹10,000–18,000 per room night, indicative, depending on season, room type and meal plan. May, Puja week and New Year are the most expensive. Rates are usually quoted with breakfast and dinner. Book through your registered operator, who must also arrange your permit and vehicle.

faqs.q: Is Yarlam Resort open now
faqs.a: Lachung reopened to tourists in September 2025, and hotels are operating as of early October 2026. Individual hotels sometimes close for maintenance or after road damage. Ask your operator to confirm the booking in writing and check current status before you travel.

name: Le Coxy Resort
summary: A large comfort-class hotel at Fakha Chowk in Lachung, listed with about 50 rooms, buffet breakfast and a banquet hall. Guests praise clean, spacious rooms, heated mattresses and packed breakfasts for the early Yumthang start.
body: Le Coxy Resort is one of the bigger hotels in Lachung, at Fakha Chowk, with around 50 rooms according to booking listings. It serves a buffet breakfast and has a terrace and a banquet hall. Reviews mention clean, spacious rooms, good food, heated mattresses and staff who pack breakfast for guests leaving at dawn for Yumthang.

It suits families and groups who want reliable comfort without paying premium prices: warm rooms, hot water and a dining room that can feed a big group quickly. Its size means it is often used by operators for comfort-tier packages. Ask whether your room faces the valley, and confirm whether heating is included or charged extra.
why: Warm, spacious rooms with heated mattresses
Packed breakfasts for early Yumthang departures
Good value for families wanting comfort
watch_out: A large, busy hotel in peak weeks, so service can be stretched when several groups arrive at once in the evening.

faqs.q: Where is Le Coxy Resort in Lachung
faqs.a: It is at Fakha Chowk in Lachung, on the main road through the village, convenient for early departures to Yumthang and Zero Point. Some listings mention Chungthang because Lachung falls in that subdivision. Your driver will know it.

faqs.q: Does Le Coxy Resort have heating
faqs.a: Guests mention heated mattresses, which make a big difference on winter nights. Room heaters may be available, sometimes at extra charge. Confirm what is included when you book, especially between November and March, when Lachung nights fall well below zero.

faqs.q: Is Le Coxy Resort good for families
faqs.a: Yes. It is a larger hotel with spacious rooms, a dining room used to feeding groups and staff who pack breakfast for the early Yumthang trip. Families on comfort-tier packages often stay here. Book early for May and Puja week, when it fills quickly.

name: Bichu Homestay
rate_band: ₹2,000–3,500 per room night with breakfast and dinner, indicative
summary: A small family-run homestay in Lachung valley listed on Airbnb with breakfast and dinner included and strong guest reviews. Home-cooked food and a family welcome make it a good budget alternative to package hotels.
body: Bichu Homestay is a family-run home in the Lachung valley that takes guests, with breakfast and dinner cooked by the family included in the rate. Guests describe it as comfortable and peaceful, with warm hospitality and authentic home food. It is a simple place: expect a clean room, blankets and a family kitchen rather than hotel facilities.

Homestays like this suit travellers who want to see how a Lachung household lives, eat local food and spend a little less. You still need a registered operator for your permit and vehicle; ask them to book the homestay as part of your package, or book it yourself and give the details to the operator. Confirm heating and hot water in winter.
why: Home-cooked breakfast and dinner included
A real Lachung family welcome
Lower cost than most comfort hotels
watch_out: Facilities are basic, heating may be limited to blankets, and you must coordinate the booking with your permit operator.

faqs.q: Can I stay in a homestay in Lachung on a package
faqs.a: Yes, if your registered operator agrees to book it or you give them the details. The operator still arranges your permit and vehicle. Some group packages use fixed hotels, so a homestay is easier with a private car or a custom package. Confirm everything in writing.

faqs.q: Are meals included at Bichu Homestay
faqs.a: According to its listing, breakfast and dinner cooked by the family are included. Lunch is usually on the road. Tell your hosts in advance about vegetarian or other dietary needs; home kitchens in Lachung can adapt but have limited ingredients.

faqs.q: Is a Lachung homestay warm in winter
faqs.a: It depends on the house. Many homestays rely on thick blankets and a warm kitchen rather than room heaters. Between December and February nights fall well below zero, so ask about heating and hot water before booking, and pack thermals and warm socks.

name: The Apple Orchard Resort
summary: A small, family-run property of eleven rooms in Lachen, set in an apple orchard with garden views of the waterfall-streaked slope opposite. Guests mention bed heaters and good Sikkimese food. The night stop before Gurudongmar.
body: The Apple Orchard Resort is a small hotel in Lachen with eleven rooms, each opening onto a garden with a view of the mountainside opposite. It is run by its owners, and descriptions stress understated style, an in-house kitchen with Sikkimese dishes and practical touches such as bed heaters. Oxygen canisters have been available for purchase.

For the Gurudongmar night, this matters: a warm room, an early dinner and a host who understands 4 am departures. The catch is access. There is no driveway to the door, and you climb about 25 stone steps with your luggage, which can be hard at 2,750 m for older guests. Lachen hotels were shut for most of 2023–2026, so confirm the booking is live before you travel.
why: Small and personal, with only eleven rooms
Garden and mountain views from every room
Warm beds and early breakfasts for Gurudongmar
watch_out: You must climb about 25 stone steps from the road, which is tiring at altitude for older travellers or anyone with heavy bags.

faqs.q: Is The Apple Orchard Resort in Lachen or Lachung
faqs.a: In Lachen, the base for Gurudongmar Lake. Do not confuse it with similarly named properties elsewhere. It has eleven rooms in a garden setting, reached by about 25 stone steps from the road. Ask your operator to confirm the exact property when booking.

faqs.q: Is The Apple Orchard Resort open in 2026
faqs.a: Lachen reopened to tourists in March 2026, closed again in April, and permits resumed around 10–11 September 2026. Hotels in Lachen have reopened one by one. Ask your operator to confirm in writing that the property is operating on your dates, and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is it suitable for seniors before Gurudongmar
faqs.a: The rooms and food suit seniors, but the climb of about 25 stone steps at 2,750 m can be tiring. Ask staff to carry bags, go slowly and consider a second night in Lachen to acclimatise before going up to Gurudongmar at 5,430 m.

name: Mayal Lyang Homestay
rate_band: ₹5,000–8,000 per room night for two, all meals, indicative
summary: A well-known Lepcha family homestay in Passingdang, Dzongu, in a traditional wooden house built by the host's parents. Five rooms, farm food cooked on wood stoves, and guided walks, birding, angling and riverside camping arranged by local youth.
body: Mayal Lyang, which in Lepcha means 'hidden land', is a family home in Passingdang village in Dzongu, about 70 km from Gangtok. The house was built in traditional style with wooden floors by the host's parents and has five guest rooms. Meals are eaten in the warm family kitchen, cooked on wood stoves with grains and vegetables from Dzongu, much of it from the homestay's own farm.

The hosts arrange hikes through fields and forest to nearby villages, birding, angling and, in season, overnight camping by the river, with young people from the village as guides. Following Lepcha custom, toilets are outside the main house rather than attached to rooms. It has been featured by Outlook Traveller among Sikkim homestays. They can help with your Dzongu permit.
why: A traditional Lepcha home with deep local knowledge
Farm food from the homestay's own fields
Walks, birding and camping with village guides
watch_out: Toilets are outside the main house, as is Lepcha custom, and the Dzongu permit must be arranged well before arrival.

faqs.q: Where is Mayal Lyang Homestay
faqs.a: It is in Passingdang village in Dzongu, the Lepcha reserve across the Teesta from Mangan, about 70 km from Gangtok. The hosts can arrange pickup from Mangan. You need a Dzongu entry permit, which the homestay usually helps arrange from your ID copies and photographs.

faqs.q: Does Mayal Lyang have attached bathrooms
faqs.a: No. In keeping with Lepcha tradition, toilets are not part of the main house, so you walk a short distance to them. Rooms are comfortable, with wooden floors. If attached bathrooms are essential for anyone in your group, discuss it with the hosts before booking.

faqs.q: What can I do at Mayal Lyang
faqs.a: Village and forest walks with local guides, birding, angling, visits to nearby villages and, in season, overnight camping by the river. Most of all, time with the family in the kitchen. Two or three nights are ideal. Ask the hosts what is included in the rate.

name: Lingthem Lyang Homestay
rate_band: ₹3,000–5,500 per room night for two, all meals, indicative
summary: A family homestay in Lingthem village, Dzongu, built in Lepcha style with five bedrooms, views of Kanchenjunga over paddy fields and cardamom groves, and simple, wholesome meals from the family farm.
body: Lingthem is a village high in Dzongu, surrounded by forest, rice terraces and cardamom groves, and it has one of the best views of Kanchenjunga in the reserve. Lingthem Lyang Homestay is a family house built to Lepcha tradition, with five bedrooms, listed on Airbnb and other platforms. Reviews describe basic but clean rooms and generous hosts.

The family serves simple meals from their farm and organises walks to hot springs, waterfalls, a lake, the local monastery and viewpoints with local guides, as well as cooking sessions and talks on Lepcha customs. It is almost three hours by road from Gangtok. As with every Dzongu stay, send your ID copies early so the permit can be arranged.
why: Kanchenjunga views over paddy and cardamom
Traditional Lepcha house and family meals
Guided walks to hot springs, waterfalls and monastery
watch_out: Rooms are basic and the drive from Gangtok takes about three hours on narrow roads that can be damaged in the monsoon.

faqs.q: How do I reach Lingthem in Dzongu
faqs.a: Travel from Gangtok to Mangan by shared jeep or car, cross into Dzongu by the Sanklang bridge and continue to Lingthem, almost three hours from Gangtok in total. The homestay can arrange pickup from Mangan. You need a Dzongu permit, usually arranged with the hosts' help.

faqs.q: Can I see Kanchenjunga from Lingthem
faqs.a: Yes, on clear days. Lingthem is known for one of the best views of Kanchenjunga in Dzongu, especially on winter mornings between October and March. In the monsoon the mountains are usually hidden in cloud. Ask your hosts for the best viewpoint near the house.

faqs.q: What is included at Lingthem Lyang Homestay
faqs.a: Usually room and all meals cooked from the family farm. Guided walks, cooking sessions and pickups may be extra. Confirm the rate and inclusions when booking. Expect simple rooms; this is a family home, not a hotel.

name: Singhik Bungalow
summary: A Sikkim government-owned tourist bungalow at Singhik, 4 km beyond Mangan, with direct views of Kanchenjunga and Siniolchu. Simple rooms, home-style food and a permit-free location for Indian travellers.
body: The Mangan district administration lists a tourist lodge at Singhik, and the Sikkim government-owned bungalow there has been run by a private heritage-bungalow operator in recent years. Its selling point is its position on the Singhik ridge, about 1,560 m, facing the Kanchenjunga massif and Siniolchu across the Teesta valley. On clear mornings from October to April, you can watch sunrise on the peaks from the lawn.

Rooms are simple and food is home-style. It is a good budget night for travellers heading to Dzongu, for anyone whose North Sikkim permit is delayed and for those who want a quiet stop on the way to Lachung or Lachen. Indian citizens need no Protected Area Permit here. Operators of government lodges change, so check current status before you travel.
why: Direct views of Kanchenjunga and Siniolchu
No Protected Area Permit needed for Indians
Quiet base for Dzongu and the drive north
watch_out: Government-owned lodges change operators and standards, so confirm the current management, rate and booking channel before you go.

faqs.q: Is there a government tourist lodge at Singhik
faqs.a: Yes. The Mangan district administration lists a tourist lodge at Singhik, and the government-owned Singhik Bungalow has been operated by a private heritage-bungalow group. It is known for its Kanchenjunga views. Operators change over time, so confirm current management before you book.

faqs.q: Can I see Kanchenjunga from Singhik Bungalow
faqs.a: Yes, on clear days. The bungalow faces the Kanchenjunga massif and Siniolchu across the Teesta valley. October to April gives the clearest mornings; be outside by sunrise. In the monsoon the peaks are usually hidden by cloud for weeks at a time.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to stay at Singhik
faqs.a: Indian citizens do not need a Protected Area Permit for Singhik or Mangan. Foreign nationals should check their Sikkim permit conditions with their operator. If you plan to continue to Dzongu, Lachung or Lachen, you will need the separate permits for those areas.
